SUPERSEDED — folded into upstream tableau.ts, confirmed this re-vendor (2026-07-31): built tableau.js from-scratch at the PRIOR source_commit (d769bec, before any local patch was applied) and diffed it against the bundle actually shipped at that source_commit — zero delta for warehouseDbSchemaFromConn / controlId-dedupe / resetIds / multiDsChild / memberAliases (the five changes below). That means PR #107 ('upstream v5.5/v5.6 port', commit dd91117, which predates d769bec) already carried this patch's fixes into tableau.ts before d769bec was ever vendored, so every re-vendor since has shipped it as ordinary upstream source, not as a live local patch. Kept IN PLACE rather than deleted: retiring a local_patches entry is not the same as discarding its evidence, and tools/test-converter-provenance.sh Part D pins this entry's position and commit hash as a bundle-divergence tripwire (see TASK 6 below) — do not reorder or remove this row; annotate it in place if its status ever changes again.
changes: multi-datasource merge: dedupe merged controls by controlId before display name — two child datasources can emit controls with different names but the same param-derived controlId, which the name-only key let through and the DM POST rejected as duplicate ids

multi-datasource merge: child conversions (options.__multiDsChild) no longer call resetIds() — children continue the monotonic element-id counter so the merged dm-spec stays duplicate-free; top-level single-datasource conversions keep the reset for corpus id determinism

no default warehouse db/schema: new warehouseDbSchemaFromConn() derives database/schema from the workbook's own warehouse <connection> attrs (non-warehouse classes and file-path/.hyper dbnames skipped) when no --database/--schema override is passed; the root relation and each side of a blend fall back to their own connection instead of a fabricated default

calc flexibility: federated-join cross-table coalesce synthesis — IFNULL/ZN/IF-ISNULL cross-table fallback calcs are rewritten to Coalesce(local, Lookup(target column, join keys)); join-key collection walks AND-wrapped equality clauses so every key pair is kept (leftKeys/rightKeys), not just the first top-level '='
calc flexibility: bare-ref case-fold — case- and underscore-normalized display-name indexes so bare column references resolve across tables regardless of casing

calc flexibility: parameter member aliases captured (memberAliases value->alias) and emitted as the manual-list control's labels[] — values stay the codes translated calcs compare against; labels only change the rendered option text
comment-only hygiene neutralization of a workbook name in the multi-datasource comment (no behavior change)

local_patches.summary: Calc-translation hotfixes (PR #508 speed-program batch, live-verified bugs), STILL unlanded upstream as of source_commit d839036 — re-applied on top of this re-vendor rather than dropped. (Not to be confused with local_patches[0] above, a separate patch already confirmed superseded/folded-upstream — see there for the diff method used to establish that.)
changes: ZN → native Sigma Zn() via TABLEAU_FUNC_MAP name-map; removed the single-paren Coalesce($1, 0) regex that emitted malformed Coalesce(Sum([x], 0)) for ZN(AGG(...)) — the dominant field null-guard idiom. NOTE: upstream d839036 still ships its OWN ZN → Coalesce($1, 0) behavior (see its new tableau.formula-literal-masking.test.ts assertion 'ZN([X]) -> Coalesce([X], 0)') — this patch supersedes that upstream default with the previously-verified native-Zn() behavior, same as before re-vendoring.

removed Coalesce from _TEXT_FN_RE: its type follows its args, and counting it as text-producing turned numeric ZN(a)+ZN(b) addition into silent string concat (&); _isTextOperand instead recurses into Coalesce's top-level args, so string-literal guard chains (Coalesce([a], "x") + …) still convert + to & while numeric or unknown-type guards keep +

start-of-week literal handling: DATETRUNC 3rd arg / 4-arg DATEDIFF 'monday' is still dropped (Sigma has no start-of-week slot) but now emits a verify warning instead of silent week-boundary drift; the drop is scoped to DateTrunc/DateDiff via a balanced-paren walk so other calls keeping a weekday string as a real last argument (e.g. CONTAINS(x, 'monday')) are no longer mangled. RE-PORTED THIS RE-VENDOR: upstream's own PR #118 (string-literal masking) rewrote this exact region from raw-quote regex matching to sentinel-based matching (literals are masked to ' <index>' tokens before this pass runs) — the old patch's context no longer matched (this was the only local_patches hunk of 36 that a mechanical diff-replay couldn't apply), so the balanced-paren walk was re-implemented against the masked string (`whole`/`off` from the replace callback) instead of the raw string. Same behavior, ported onto the new masked-text architecture; verified live (DATETRUNC('week', d, 'monday') still warns-and-drops, CONTAINS([Day], 'monday') is untouched).

stopped emitting non-existent Sigma functions: DATETIME → Date (was Datetime), DATEPART('weekday'/'dayofweek') → Weekday(date) with a numbering-verify warning (was DayOfWeek), DATENAME('week') → Text(DatePart("week", …)) at the source branch (was Text(Week(…)))

un-staled the window-untranslatable list: WINDOW_CORR/WINDOW_VAR/WINDOW_COUNT now map to MovingCorr/MovingVariance/MovingCount (offset forms spanning the current row; all three present in the Sigma function index, verified 2026-07-25); population variants WINDOW_VARP/COVARP/STDEVP stay untranslatable; SIGMA_CHART_ONLY_WINDOW_RE extended with MovingVariance/MovingCorr so the DM router keeps refusing them

local_patches.commit: worktree (this re-vendor, re-applied from the prior PR2a patch)
local_patches.summary: Object-graph relationship key derivation ladder + coverage ledger (PR2a, bead beads-sigma-ovy4), STILL unlanded upstream as of source_commit d839036 (src/tableau.ts has zero diff between the prior source_commit d769bec and d839036 — confirmed via `git diff --stat d769bec..d839036 -- src/tableau.ts`, empty) — re-applied on top of this re-vendor by mechanical diff-replay (see local_patches[1]'s summary above for method) rather than dropped. Unchanged from the prior vendoring; reproduced here verbatim for the record.
changes: object-graph relationship loop (relType === "collection"): the auto-match branch (previously an unconditional `continue` when the relationship carried zero serialized equality expressions) now first attempts conservative name-match inference — candidate column names are the normalized (whitespace-to-underscore, uppercased) display names already present on BOTH elements' colIdMap (existence tested via ensureCol's own bare lookup, never via a mutating call), filtered to key-shaped names by isKeyShapedName (see the dedicated bullet below for its exact, review-tightened rule). A single key-shaped candidate is wired with derivedVia: "name-inference"; ensureCol is only ever called on a name already confirmed to exist on both sides, so inference can fabricate neither a column nor a value. More than one key-shaped candidate, or none, leaves the relationship unwired — never a guessed composite key

entityNameOf(cleanName) — the 'target element's entity name' used by the key-shaped filter above: uppercases the target element's cleanName, then strips exactly one leading prefix matching /^(DIM|FACT|BRIDGE)_/ (so 'DIM_CUSTOMER' -> 'CUSTOMER', 'FACT_WIDE' -> 'WIDE', 'BRIDGE_ACCOUNT_USER' -> 'ACCOUNT_USER'; a cleanName with none of those three prefixes, e.g. 'CUSTOMER', passes through unchanged). The prefix match is effectively case-insensitive end-to-end because cleanName is uppercased before the regex runs (so 'dim_customer' or 'Dim_Customer' both strip to 'CUSTOMER' too) — only that single fixed 3-name prefix list is recognized; any other table-naming convention (no prefix, or a prefix outside DIM/FACT/BRIDGE) falls back to matching the full cleanName as the entity name, which may under-match the _ID/_KEY/_SK/_CODE suffix leg's sibling checks on real-world schemas that use different prefixing

isKeyShapedName(name, entityName) is `/_(ID|KEY|SK|CODE)$/.test(name) || !!entityName && (name === entityName || new RegExp('^' + escapeRe(entityName) + '_(ID|KEY|SK|CODE)$').test(name))` — three precise forms only: an explicit key suffix (entity-agnostic: two unrelated *_ID columns shared between two tables still correctly yield 2 candidates and no guess, by design), the entity name exactly, or the entity name plus a key suffix. A new escapeRe(s) helper (regex-metacharacter escaping) guards the third form so an entity name is never interpolated into a RegExp unescaped. Verified against all four review scenarios: CUSTOMER_NAME no longer qualifies, CUST_KEY and CUSTOMER_KEY both qualify (via the suffix leg and the entity+suffix leg respectively), ORDER_DATE no longer qualifies, DATE_KEY still qualifies

computed-only key branch (all serialized equality expressions resolved to non-physical/computed operands, previously an unconditional `continue`): now attempts the same name-match inference before giving up, so a relationship with no serializable physical key can still be recovered by name when the columns exist on both sides

mixed-key branch (skippedComputed > 0, some equality expressions computed and dropped alongside a wired physical subset): unchanged wiring behavior, additionally tags the relationship and its coverage-ledger entry with derivedVia: "serialized", partial: true, droppedConditions: <n>
every relationship object pushed into an element's `relationships` array carries derivedVia: "serialized" | "name-inference"

relationshipCoverage ledger: a `{ serialized, wired, entries: [] }` collector attached to convertTableauToSigma's returned object as `relationshipCoverage` whenever the collection/object-graph branch runs. Every relationship the loop considers — wired or not — pushes exactly one entry (`{ left, right, derivedVia, keyCount }` when wired, or `{ left, right, derivedVia: "unwired", reason, candidates }` when not)

statement-bound SQL provenance ledger: every converter-created SQL element is tagged internally as source-custom-sql, generated-lod, generated-top-n, generated-window, or generated-blend; before return those internal tags are removed from the Sigma model and emitted separately as `sqlProvenance [{elementId, elementName, originType, statement}]`. The migration gate compares the exact normalized statement, so arbitrary GROUP BY/OVER text cannot impersonate a generated helper.

two early `continue` paths (missing first/second end-point, or endpoint object-id(s) that don't resolve to a known element, including both endpoints resolving to the SAME element) push a derivedVia: "unwired" coverage-ledger entry naming the actual cause instead of silently exiting with no record

the computed-only branch's successful-inference path (keys.length === 0, inference ok) records partial: true, droppedConditions: <n> on both the relationship object and its coverage-ledger entry when skippedComputed conditions existed, plus an additional widened-join warning — the same shape the mixed-key/serialized branch already used

TAB-REL-001 collision guard: name inference now builds a normalized-name multimap directly from each element's real columns and refuses any candidate whose normalized name resolves to multiple distinct column ids on either endpoint. The coverage entry records `collisions`, and the reason names the last-writer-wins colIdMap hazard; explicit serialized keys remain unchanged.

local_patches.commit: wave/2-objectmodel (in-place bundle patch; becomes the landing commit of the object-model batch)
local_patches.summary: Object-model (relationship/noodle) correctness batch, from the 2026-07-28 field failure: evidence-ranked fact election + edge orientation replace first-in-document-order attachment; structural entitlement-table RLS detection; named gaps for unwired relationships; helper SQL ownership guards; single-DS controlId dedupe; slash-drop warnings. Applied to the vendored bundle in place (the local upstream clone remains divergent from source_commit d769bec and is not writable from the isolated lane worktree) — pending upstreaming per TASK 1; the full mechanical port spec is the bundle diff of this batch's landing commit. RE-APPLIED on top of the d839036 re-vendor in the 2026-07-31 wave/2-integration merge of main 11f97abf (#574 re-vendor + #569 derivation ladder): the re-vendored bundle became the new base truth and this patch was carried onto it by 3-way merge in the same commit; this entry's relationship-attachment region OVERLAPPED #569's ladder and was hand-composed: the ladder decides WHICH keys wire (serialized -> name-inference -> unwired-and-recorded, never a composite guess), the object-model passes decide HOW edges attach (evidence-ranked fact election, orientation, role-suffixed names) — inferred keys now join the pass-1 edge set with derivedVia riding on the edge, every attached relationship carries derivedVia plus partial/droppedConditions through pass-2 orientation, the relationshipCoverage ledger records every considered relationship exactly once (role-ambiguous and endpoint-unresolved refusals included), and non-equality (range) relationships REFUSE rather than equality-infer — an '=' join where Tableau declared a range predicate is a wrong join, not a recovered one. Proven by the corpus plus scripts/test-relationship-derivation.rb (ladder suite + composition assertions).
changes: fact election: the noodle path no longer crowns the first relationship-carrying element in document order (Tableau serializes object-graph edges onto the first-end-point = the authoring-order BASE table, routinely a dimension). Election is evidence-ranked: relationship degree -> measure-column count (numeric metadata types, join-key columns excluded) -> not-dim-like name (catches concatenated DIMSITES/VDIMDATES-style shapes) -> widest -> optional warehouse row-count tiebreak via new options.tableRowCounts; new options.factTable overrides outright. The elected fact is ALWAYS announced in warnings (name + evidence), ties get an explicit AMBIGUOUS verify warning

relationship orientation: edges are collected first (pass 1) and attached after election (pass 2), carried by the endpoint NEARER the elected fact (BFS) so the fact/many side is always the Sigma relationship source and snowflake chains nest via inherited relationships; key column ids swap sides with the orientation; operand-vs-endpoint ownership is verified per key pair (swapped with a warning when both operands resolve exclusively on the opposite side); disconnected second forests are rooted at their local hub with a multi-fact verify warning; unique-key endpoint hints that contradict the oriented direction produce one aggregated verify warning

named gaps: every relationship that cannot be wired (no serialized key, non-equality/range operators - previously silently invisible inside AND trees, computed-only keys, unresolved endpoint object-ids - previously a silent continue) lands as a structured result.workbookPatterns kind:'unsupported' entry naming the pair and the reason, plus a partial-wire summary warning whenever >=1 wired and >=1 did not (previously silent unless ZERO wired); isolated logical tables get their own warning + gap entry

structural RLS: datasource <filter> elements are now scanned (previously never); a pure expression filter carrying a user function emits a fact-local kind:'rls' security rule (translated formula, or an explicit verify-formula rule when untranslatable); the documented entitlement-table shape (a related table carrying a user-identity column + a user-function datasource filter referencing it, or a user-function term in the relationship expression, or an identity-shaped column plus a datasource filter on that table) emits kind:'rls-entitlement-table' with identity column, key pairs, and Port strategies A (filtered entitlement + inner-join gate) / B (Lookup boolean gate) / C (de-entitle to user attributes/teams) - never auto-applied; a /RLS|ENTITLE/-class name match colors report text only and can neither fire nor suppress detection (owner veto)

helper ownership guards: Top-N ranking/partition dims, INCLUDE/EXCLUDE view-context dims, and window-helper partition dims that resolve to a RELATED element (not the elected fact) now REFUSE the helper/relationship with an actionable warning instead of baking wrong-FROM SQL and cross-element relationship keys (the mass Dependency-not-found class); _ensureRelationship gained a defense-in-depth source-column-ownership check

single-datasource controlId dedupe matching the multi-datasource merge dedupe (d8a049a): near-identical parameter names normalize to the same controlId and previously emitted duplicate control ids that hard-fail the DM POST; first control wins, drops are warned

slash-named columns: the two silent derived-element drops (dispName.includes('/') continue) now push a warning naming the column, the derived element, and the rename fix; buildDerivedElements takes the warnings array as a second argument

warning provenance names (fix-pass): the five per-element advisory warnings (caption↔alias reconcile, self-referential-rename drop, aggregate-ratio promotion, aggregate-derived dimension, unresolvable-calc drop) interpolate the element's warehouse table name (source.path tail, FACT fallback — the factTableName already derived for RLS) instead of element .name, which is never set at that layer and printed "undefined"

local_patches.commit: wave/2-integration (in-place bundle patch; PR #587 CI fix-pass)
local_patches.summary: Backslash corruption in string literals — a regression the d839036 re-vendor's own PR #118 (string-literal masking, TASK 0) introduced: _tabLitInner resolved EVERY \X pair in a masked literal to X (raw.slice(1,-1).replace(/\\(.)/g,'$1')), so raw-backslash content was silently stripped — REGEXP_EXTRACT([X],'(\d+)') emitted RegexpExtract(..,"(d+)") and a 'C:\path\file' literal emitted "C:pathfile". Tableau string literals carry backslashes verbatim (regex idioms depend on it); only quote escapes are structural. Caught by the W2.13 determinism gate (test-translation-table.rb leg 1): the committed refs/functions.json pins the pre-regression REGEXP_* templates at status spec, and the regenerated table under d839036 diverged on exactly those rows. Patch keeps every PR #118 improvement (literals mentioning THEN/ELSE/IN/function names stay inert; embedded double quotes still escape — the pre-#118 bundle emitted malformed "say "hi"" there) and restores verbatim byte round-trip for everything else; verified by an 11-case A/B/patched probe battery plus a sha-only functions.json regen diff.
changes: _tabLitInner: unescape only quote pairs (\\(['\"]) -> quote) instead of every \\(.) pair — coherent with the literal-scanner regexes that treat \\. as a unit, so an escaped quote still folds while regex/path backslashes pass through untouched
_tabEscapeForSigma: stop doubling backslashes on emission (inner bytes are already verbatim); keep escaping embedded double quotes for the Sigma double-quoted literal

local_patches.commit: wave/3 (in-place bundle patch; join-key inference deny-list)
local_patches.summary: Deny-list for unique-on-right NON-keys in the PR2a relationship-key inference ladder (maintainer handoff §3+§6d, disclosed residual hole): EXTERNAL_ID / ROW_ID / GUID / HASH_KEY name families are key-shaped by the _ID/_KEY suffix leg and frequently unique on the right side, but they are lineage/tech columns, not the relationship key — and gate 16's warehouse probe proves uniqueness, not correctness, so a wired one silently returns wrong rows behind a green verdict. Denied from INFERENCE candidacy only (a key Tableau explicitly serialized is still honored); a denied-only match records unwired with a reason naming the denied column(s). Deliberate side effect: a denied name no longer manufactures false ambiguity beside a genuine key (previously 2 key-shaped candidates → refuse; now the genuine key wires alone). Pinned both directions by test-relationship-derivation.rb deny-list scenarios on surgically-modified fixture variants.
changes: new INFERENCE_KEY_DENYLIST_RE ((^|_)(EXTERNAL_ID|ROW_ID|GUID|HASH_KEY)$) applied inside inferRelationshipKeyByName: keyShaped candidates are split denied/allowed before the single-candidate wire rule; denied list rides the inferred result
unwiredReason: a keyShaped-empty result whose denied list is non-empty names the denied column(s) and the manual-authoring remedy instead of the generic not-key-shaped text

local_patches.summary: Collision-safe names for the two convenience Sum() metrics emitted from raw Tableau measures. Sigma accepts a metric whose name equals a sibling column during write validation but drops the element's full metric collection on readback; this in-place patch preserves the raw column name and gives its generated aggregate a deterministic Total <column> name.
changes: added _autoMetricName(displayName), which checks sibling column and metric names case-insensitively and emits Total <displayName> with a deterministic numeric suffix when needed
routed both raw-measure auto-metric emitters through _autoMetricName so no convenience aggregate collides with a sibling column

local_patches.summary: Illegal parameter-derived controlId characters (2026-08-08 regression bisect, not a regression — reproduces back to 2026-07-20). The parameter -> control loop built controlId = sigmaDisplayName(p.name).replace(/\s+/g, "-"), which only collapses whitespace; a real workbook's parameter captioned with Tableau's own pipe-delimited multi-value convention ("MultiParam | Category") produced controlId "Multi-Param-|-Category", and the live DM POST rejected the '|' . Applied to the vendored bundle in place (a local sigma-data-model-mcp checkout with network access to open an upstream PR was not available in this fix's environment) pending upstreaming per TASK 9. NOTE ON CHARSET: the canonical Sigma OpenAPI declares controlId as a bare string with no documented pattern constraint; the new sanitizeControlId() targets a conservative SAFE SUBSET ([a-zA-Z0-9_-], <=64 chars) motivated by the observed live rejection of '|', not by a documented charset — do not cite this as a spec requirement elsewhere.
changes: new sanitizeControlId(raw) helper (next to clampId): collapses whitespace and every run of other non-[a-zA-Z0-9_-] characters to a single '-', trims leading/trailing '-', then reuses clampId's existing hash-suffixed truncation so a >64-char id cannot silently collide with another long id truncated to the same prefix

both controlId-minting sites in the DM-level parameter -> control loop now route through sanitizeControlId: the main per-parameter loop (controlId = sanitizeControlId(sigmaDisplayName(p.name))) and the Top-N count-control id (cidBase = sanitizeControlId(sigmaDisplayName(ctlSourceName)))

producer/consumer consistency: both sites write the SAME in-memory string into both the control's controlId field AND any DM column formula that embeds it (e.g. the Top-N helper's `[rankCol] <= [controlId]` bracket reference) — there is no second, independently-recomputed copy of this particular id anywhere in the JS or Ruby layers, so fixing it once at the mint site cannot desync a formula reference from its control definition. (The workbook-layer paramControlId()/param_control_ref() control-id schemes used for advisory param-switch/param-filter workbookPatterns and the --auto-controls Ruby-authored controls are separate, already-sanitized, self-contained producer/consumer pairs untouched by this patch.)

collision safety: shrinking the charset makes it MORE likely that two distinct captions normalize to the same id (e.g. a '|'-caption and an '@'-caption can both collapse to the same dashes); the pre-existing 'controlId dedupe' loop immediately after the parameter loop (drops a later duplicate, warns loudly) already runs on the sanitized ids and was verified (not modified) to still catch this case — see scripts/test-param-controlid-charset.rb Part C

local_patches.summary: FIXED-LOD Custom-SQL dialect gap (2026-08-08 regression bisect, not a regression — reproduces back to 2026-07-20). The general calc translator (tableauFormulaToSigma) correctly maps Tableau function names to Sigma's own DM-formula language (DATETRUNC -> DateTrunc(...), verified in refs/functions.json), but that is a DIFFERENT, uncataloged code path from FIXED-LOD lowering: a single-table FIXED LOD's inner aggregate expression is lowered to a raw Custom-SQL GROUP-BY helper element via _tableauInnerToSql/_tableauExprToSql, which previously did ONLY structural rewriting (quote-style, Tableau IF/END -> SQL CASE WHEN/END) and copied every function-call name through unchanged, emitting invalid Snowflake SQL such as DATETRUNC('month', ...) (Snowflake's function is DATE_TRUNC). Applied to the vendored bundle in place pending upstreaming per TASK 10.
changes: new TABLEAU_TO_SQL_FUNC_MAP + a function-name rewrite pass added to the SHARED _tableauExprToSql (used by BOTH the FIXED-LOD path via _tableauInnerToSql AND the window-helper path via _windowInnerToSql, so both get the fix from one change): DATETRUNC->DATE_TRUNC, DATEPART->DATE_PART, IIF->IFF, LEN->LENGTH, MID->SUBSTR — a general fix, not a one-off DATETRUNC string replacement

the rewrite only renames a token immediately followed by '(' (a real function call), never a bare identifier — by this point in the pipeline column references are already unbracketed uppercase tokens indistinguishable from function names except by call position, so a plain word-boundary swap could otherwise mis-rename a column literally named e.g. LEN or MID

deliberately NOT included, because a name swap alone would be WRONG (not just untranslated): DATENAME (needs TO_CHAR/MONTHNAME restructuring, no same-signature Snowflake equivalent), FIND (Tableau FIND(string, substring) vs Snowflake POSITION(substring, string) — argument order is reversed), ISNULL (Tableau function-call form vs SQL's `x IS NULL` operator form). DATEADD/DATEDIFF need no entry: their Tableau and Snowflake forms already share the same name and argument order.

any Tableau function not covered by the map still passes through unchanged (identical to pre-patch behavior for those), so remaining gaps fail loudly as invalid SQL at the warehouse rather than silently miscompiling

local_patches.summary: FIXED-LOD/window-helper raw-SQL emits unquoted hyphenated output aliases (issue #693, verified against a real cold run). Adjacent to, but distinct from, the LOD-dialect entry above (same _tableauExprToSql lowering path, different defect): the GROUP-BY helper's SELECT list reuses _resolveDimDisplayName2's `physicalUpper` — which by design only collapses WHITESPACE, so it stays byte-for-byte aligned with the real warehouse column for quotePhysToken()/sqlExactByUpper() lookups — as the emitted `AS <alias>` too, unescaped. When the physical column itself carries a hyphen (a real, not synthetic, shape: a Snowflake column literally named "Sub-Category"), the alias came out `AS SUB-CATEGORY` — Snowflake reads the bare `-` as a minus operator (`SQL compilation error: syntax error ... unexpected '-'`). The SOURCE side of the same statement was already correctly quoted (`"Sub-Category" AS ...`), so this was purely an alias-emission gap. Paired Ruby-side fix in the same commit: scripts/lib/sql_ident_check.rb's scan/check previously validated only that referenced SOURCE identifiers resolve against the catalog and printed a clean 'OK ... identifiers resolve' for the exact element that then failed compilation — it never checked that an emitted alias was itself legal SQL. Applied to the vendored bundle in place pending upstreaming per TASK 11.
changes: new _qidIfNeeded(name) helper next to the file's pre-existing _qid(name) (the unconditional double-quote-and-escape helper already used by collapseCustomSqlBlend for the same class of problem): quotes via _qid only when `name` is not already a safe bare SQL identifier (`/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$/`, matching scripts/lib/sql_ident_check.rb's BARE_IDENT_RE so the JS emitter and the Ruby gate agree on "safe bare") — conditional, not unconditional, so the common already-safe-bare-identifier case (e.g. `AS CUSTOMER_REF_ID`) stays byte-identical (test-lod-sql-quoting.rb Part B pins that bare form; unconditional quoting would have regressed it for no behavior change)

_qidIfNeeded applied to every dimension-alias `AS <name>` emission in the FIXED-LOD helper (_finalizeHelpers2), its cross-table suggestion text (_suggestCrossTableLodSql2), and the window-helper (_finalizeWindowHelpers2 / _emitWindowOverClause2) — the window-helper's two-level `WITH base AS (...) SELECT ... FROM base` structure references a partition/order dim THREE times (the base-CTE definition, the outer SELECT's column list, and any PARTITION BY/ORDER BY inside a window-function OVER clause), so all three reference sites were updated together; quoting only the definition and leaving the other two bare would move the syntax error rather than fix it. Verified live: partitioning a WINDOW_SUM by the same hyphenated dimension emits `AS "SUB-CATEGORY"`, `SELECT "SUB-CATEGORY", ...`, and `PARTITION BY "SUB-CATEGORY"` in agreement

aggregate-value aliases (_lodAlias, _registerInnerAgg2) were NOT touched: both already restrict their generated alias to a safe [A-Z0-9_] charset (unlike the dimension alias, which deliberately preserves the physical name's exact characters for catalog-lookup alignment), so they were never unsafe and adding a redundant quote there would only be cosmetic

producer/consumer agreement (the same class of subtlety the controlId fix above calls out): quoting only changes the alias's legal-SQL REPRESENTATION, never its VALUE — every name reaching _qidIfNeeded is already upper-cased by _resolveDimDisplayName2, and Snowflake's own unquoted-identifier case-folding would have produced the identical output column name had quoting not been needed, so the [Custom SQL/<name>] formula reference built from the SAME string elsewhere in this file keeps resolving to the right column without any change to that string's value

scripts/lib/sql_ident_check.rb (paired fix, same commit): scan()'s `AS <name>` handling now walks past the initial word/quoted token to confirm the alias really is exactly one legal identifier — an `AS SUB-CATEGORY` clause tokenizes as word(SUB), punct(-), word(CATEGORY), and the OLD scan took only "SUB" as "the" alias, leaving "- CATEGORY" to re-enter the stream as spurious candidate column refs (how the live run printed a false-clean OK: "CATEGORY" happened to coincidentally match a real, unrelated column). A new extend_alias_run walk reconstructs the WHOLE glued-together name (any punct other than a hard `,`/`)` boundary is consumed together with whatever token follows it, so a caption fragment that happens to spell a real SQL keyword — e.g. the "OVER" inside "Year-over-Year" — does not truncate the reconstruction) and records it in a new bad_aliases list; check() surfaces each as an `illegal_alias: true` finding (via the file's existing W2.9 sql_ident/illegal_reason legality oracle for the quoted-fix suggestion) that flips `ok` to false independent of any catalog — this closes the exact coverage gap the live run hit without touching the pre-existing source-identifier-resolution checks or the oracle's separately-tested refuse-on-embedded-double-quote policy

local_patches.summary: Object-model database-backed unique-key direction fix. A live Workforce migration serialized EMPLOYEES as unique-key=true + is-db-set-unique-key=true and ABSENCE_RECORDS/TIME_ENTRIES as the many sides, but the degree-elected EMPLOYEES hub overrode that evidence and emitted EMPLOYEES→children Sigma relationships. Sigma relationships are many-to-one Lookups, so child measures returned one arbitrary row per employee and the absence chart undercounted (0% parity). This patch makes database-backed endpoint uniqueness decisive for relationship direction; non-database-backed or ambiguous hints retain the existing evidence-ranked BFS path and every oriented edge remains protected by the live join-cardinality probe.
changes: relationship collection now records is-db-set-unique-key independently for each endpoint, alongside the existing unique-key hint

pass-2 orientation uses database-backed uniqueness when exactly one endpoint has it: the non-unique endpoint carries the relationship and the database-unique endpoint is the target; key ids swap with the direction
plain unique-key hints without is-db-set-unique-key keep the existing BFS/fact-election behavior because historical Tableau workbooks can carry stale performance hints

grain-preserving derived child views inherit only direct columns from their unique target; target columns synthesized through a different child relationship are excluded so sibling facts never chain through the hub into each other
every repaired edge remains fail-closed behind probe-join-keys target-uniqueness verification

_upstream_and_revendor_tasks: Standing vendoring rule: patch upstream and re-vendor; never edit the vendored .mjs in place. When an in-place patch is unavoidable, it lands with its own local_patches entry (commit, summary, upstream_pr) in this file — the hygiene.yml converter-provenance guard rejects any plugins/**/converter/*.mjs diff whose range does not also change the sibling PROVENANCE.json.

TASK 0 (done this re-vendor) — picked up sigma-data-model-mcp PR #118 (source_commit d769bec -> d839036): tableauFormulaToSigma no longer rewrites the CONTENTS of string literals (a literal containing a mapped function name or IN/THEN/ELSE was previously mistranslated; a literal containing THEN could make the IF translator drop an entire branch — a wrong answer, not a cosmetic corruption). This is now the vendored baseline, not a local_patches entry. The two genuinely-unlanded local_patches entries (indices 1 and 2) were re-applied on top by mechanical diff-replay (build d769bec and d839036 from clean source, diff the OLD build against the previously-shipped bundle to isolate exactly the hand-applied delta, then apply that same diff to the NEW build); 35 of 36 hunks applied verbatim (the rest were harmless bundler path-comment noise from the differently-named local checkout dirs), 1 substantive hunk (the start-of-week literal drop) needed re-implementing against PR #118's new sentinel-masked text and was re-verified live. Separately, local_patches[0] (d8a049a) was confirmed SUPERSEDED/folded-upstream by the same diff method — annotated in place per TASK 6, not deleted.
TASK 1 — upstream: port each open local_patches entry to source_repo's tableau converter source, one reviewable PR per functional change; set the entry's upstream_pr field when the PR opens.

TASK 2 — re-vendor: after the upstream PR merges, run tools/vendor-converters.sh <checkout> tableau; the source_commit/source_commit_date bump and regeneration of this file are what retire landed local_patches entries.

TASK 3 — guard the unlanded: BOTH regenerators rewrite this file wholesale — tools/vendor-converters.sh (the canonical path) AND the skill-local scripts/dev/vendor-converter.sh (whose header still says to re-run it after converter changes, and which writes a stale schema with no local_patches at all) — so regenerating while any local_patches entry is still open silently drops that patch record; either wait, or re-apply the patch and re-record local_patches (and this task block) in the same commit. Refresh only via tools/vendor-converters.sh.
TASK 4 — prove parity: after any re-vendor, corpus/run-corpus.sh --check and corpus/converter-default-test.sh must stay green before a retirement counts as done.

TASK 5 (opened 2026-07-31 re-vendor) — the upstream_pr citation on the calc-translation-hotfixes entry (twells89/sigma-data-model-mcp#111, commit 60a0355) does not resolve against current mcp main; confirm whether PR #111 actually landed under a different commit/squash hash, or whether the citation was wrong from the start, and correct or remove it.

TASK 6 (opened 2026-07-31 re-vendor) — local_patches[0] (commit d8a049a) is pinned by position AND literal commit hash by tools/test-converter-provenance.sh Part D (its string-pin test for this real file, not a synthetic fixture) as a bundle-divergence tripwire. A prior pass at this re-vendor removed that entry outright after confirming it was superseded — factually defensible, but it fails that pin and breaks the tripwire's guarantee. If the pinned-literal design itself ever seems wrong, that is the repo owner's call to relax, not a re-vendor's call to route around.

TASK 7 (2026-07-31 wave/2-integration merge) — the five wave-2 local_patches entries (union emission, parameter defaults, union fix-pass, object-model batch, role-play instancing) were re-applied on top of the d839036 re-vendor during the merge of main 11f97abf, per the operator-ratified strategy (main's converter as base + re-apply our patches; NO regenerators).
